newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-LANCHASIRE WIN DESPITE WELCH HAUL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LANCHASIRE WIN DESPITE WELCH HAUL.

text.p: A brilliant five-wicket haul for Warwickshire by Graeme Welch did not stop Lancashire completing a thrilling three-wicket win on the third day of an English county cricket league match on Friday.
Lancashire only needed 88 for victory after they had bowled Warwickshire out for 310 earlier in the day.
But Welch and Allan Donald ripped through the home side's top order to give them some hope before Warren Hegg and Gary Yates steered Lancashire to 91 for seven.

Hampshire's former England batsman John Stephenson and Matthew Keech shared an unbroken sixth-wicket partnership of 100 to make honours even in the third day of their match against Middlesex at Lord's.
At the close of play, Middlesex were on 91 for one, 227 runs ahead, Hampshire having declared at tea at 306 for five shortly after they had gained their third batting point and avoided the follow-on.
Middlesex lost Paul Weekes cheaply but South African Jacques Kallis was 49 not out at the close and Mike Gatting was on 37.
Northamptonshire youngster Michael Davies claimed a notable first ever scalp in first class cricket when he had Worcestershire captain Tom Moody caught at slip in the match at Northampton.
Slow left armer Davies, 21, has been highly touted by Northants and finished with three for 75 as Worcestershire ended the day on 219 for five for an overall lead of 367.
Russell Warren had earlier scored a brilliant 174 not out to help Northants declare on 403 for five.
Former England player John Morris scored a half century to ensure Durham managed to take Surrey into the final day at The Oval.

The visitors followed on 214 behind after their first innings collapsed to 136 all out, but solid resistance second time around, particularly from Morris (53), Martin Speight and Jonathan Lewis, ensured they did not go down without a fight.
When Robin Weston was out to the last ball of the day Durham were 241 for seven _ only 27 ahead _ and Surrey will admit the public for free on the final day in anticipation of shortened proceedings.
A career best of 155 by Mohammed Waseem carried Pakistan A to 365 in their match against Yorkshire at Headingley.
The captain batted for a little over five hours, faced 223 balls and hit 21 boundaries as he dominated a seventh-wicket partnership of 178 in 57 overs with the patient Javaid Qadeer.
Martyn Moxon and Michael Vaughan reached 37 without loss in Yorkshire's second innings at the close.
